newsitem.title: USA: Group says Badger should seek sale.
newsitem.headline: Group says Badger should seek sale.

text.p: A group including Bomarko Inc said Thursday it plans to call on the management and board of Badger Paper Mills Inc to consider selling Badger or its assets as a way of giving maximum value to shareholders.

In a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission, the group said it recently reevaluated the risks and prospects of its investment in Badger as the company continued to suffer substantial operating losses.

The group said it believes the most viable strategy by which it and other stockholders can limit the risk of further substantial losses to their investment may be to pursue a prompt sale of the Peshtigo, Wis., company or its assets.

If Badger is offered for sale, the group said "it might or might not offer to acquire the issuer or some or all of its assets." But it added that it was not its intention to acquire the company in making the suggestion that Badger be sold.
As part of its objectives to raise shareholder value, the group said it might seek a change in the company's board and management or by-laws.
It said it may also buy more shares to add to its 14.2 percent stake to influence management, promote the sale of the company or protect its investment.
Bomarko is a Plymouth, Ind., maker of coated and printed paper products.
